evidence.excerpt: page-1.json: created 2026-02-27T00:06:25Z, pushed 2026-03-04T23:02:41Z, 89 stars, 34 forks, MIT license, no primary language.

25 commits: 'Add 5 PM skills: LinkedIn writer, idea validator, prompt engineer, design reviewer, status updates' (2026-02-27), 'Remove 15 extra skills, add MIT LICENSE and badges' (2026-03-03), 'Enhance all 5 skills with targeted improvements for their biggest gaps' (2026-03-04).
Root: CONTRIBUTING.md (2002 B), LICENSE (1069 B), README.md (6768 B), skills/ (dir), templates/ (dir) — skills directory and the SKILL template location both exist as the README claims.

'5 production-ready Claude Code skills for product managers. Drop them in .claude/skills/ and they work immediately.' Table names all five with per-skill SKILL.md paths; setup includes a verification step ('ls .claude/skills/').

counter_evidence.excerpt: 'Remove 15 extra skills' is a curation decision — the maintainer cut scope to 5 polished skills rather than shipping 20 shallow ones; 'Improve setup instructions with one-liner install, verification, and troubleshooting' shows usability iteration.

The 'How to Create Your Own Skill' section is a genuine 5-step methodology with a full SKILL.md template inline, plus design rationale: 'CLAUDE.md loads every session; skills load only when triggered.'
CONTRIBUTING.md and templates/ exist, backing the contribution workflow the README describes — infrastructure beyond a one-shot content dump.

strongest_counter_evidence: Deliberate scope-cut from 20 to 5 skills with subsequent per-skill enhancement passes is the opposite of mass-generation padding
Three install options plus a verification command make setup fully reproducible
Inline skill-authoring guide and template constitute original teaching structure, not boilerplate
counter_evidence_review.review_notes: Negative reading rests on the re-dated commit timeline (skill adds dated into Sep 2026 that were 'removed' by a commit dated Mar 2026) shared with sibling repos — a simulated-cadence pattern. Against that, the surviving content is curated, the claimed 5 skills and template are structurally corroborated, and the editorial commits describe real quality work. Prompt/skill libraries are legitimate deliverables under the fairness rules.

evidence_conflicts: Parent-chain order vs author dates is incoherent: 16 skill-add commits dated 2026-03-10..2026-09-12 (some in the future) are ancestors of the 'Remove 15 extra skills' commit dated 2026-03-03, and pushed_at is 2026-03-04 — history was re-dated.
Same-second batch commits across siblings: 'Polish all skills and README for professional tone' 2026-03-04T23:04:13Z here vs 23:04:15/23:04:17 in pm-claude-code-setup and pm-prompt-library.
